title: Which Rényi entropies have alternating heat derivatives? No order survives, and the first failing derivative order by order
shortTitle: No Rényi order survives the heat-flow hierarchy
oneLine: One density defeats every order; collision entropy first fails at the fourth derivative
abstract: Add Gaussian noise to a random quantity and its entropy rises, ever more slowly. It was conjectured that every higher time derivative of Shannon entropy along this heat flow alternates in sign; Gu and Sellke disproved this at the fifth derivative. Wu, Yu and Guo asked the same for Rényi entropy of every order α: which orders keep every sign, and, for each derivative, which orders keep that sign? Following the earlier Evidence Press classification for Tsallis entropy, where order two is the one survivor, this candidate proves that no Rényi order in (0, ∞] keeps every sign: the logarithm removes the exception. A single smooth density on the line breaks the hierarchy for all orders at one time, and for orders bounded away from zero it can be strongly log-concave. For collision entropy (order 2) the first three signs hold for every input and the fourth fails; in dimension 4 and above the third already fails. Every derivative from the sixth on fails at every order; the third fails for orders up to 0.377 and above 2; the fourth for orders up to 0.849; the fifth outside (1.19, 1.75). With Wu, Yu and Guo's positive results this fixes the first failing derivative on most of the order axis: 2 above order 3, 3 up to 0.377 and on (2, 3], 4 from about 0.389 to 0.849 and at order 2, and 5 near Shannon entropy. Order 2 is the largest order whose third derivative has a universal sign. Among entropies of the form ∫Φ(p), only quadratic ones keep every sign. Limits: four gaps remain in the map; the common density is shown to exist, not written down; Shannon failures are inherited from Gu–Sellke and Zou et al. AI-assisted, unrefereed candidate; no external peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification is claimed.

evidence: A 19-page paper with a context-first introduction, written proofs, limits, open problems and an AI-use statement. Nine Python programs accompany it, and every check raises an error on failure, even under python -O: six exact rational or interval certificates on the standard library (two circle coefficients, the fourth derivative at order 2, the third sign in dimension 4, the valley rows for derivatives 3 to 6 with controls that must not certify, and interval certificates for the sixth derivative on orders up to 3 and the fifth above 1.75), a shared Fourier-jet module, and two optional sympy/mpmath programs (exploratory valley thresholds and a direct sign cross-check). A clean replay in optimised mode reproduced every recorded output byte for byte in about half a minute; a perturbed enclosure makes check_alpha2.py fail; Linux CI reruns all eight programs, comparing the six certificates exactly and the two mpmath outputs within a declared relative tolerance of 1e-6.

keyResults: Theorems 4.1 and 4.4 (proof): no Rényi order α in (0, ∞] keeps every alternating sign along the heat flow; one smooth density violates a sign for every order at one time, strongly log-concave for orders bounded away from zero, in every dimension.

Theorem 5.1 (proof and exact certificate): at order 2 the first three signs hold for every input and the fourth fails; at variance time 1/32 the fourth derivative of the witness lies between 0.0249 and 0.025. In dimension 4 and above the third sign fails.

Theorem 6.1 (proof and certificates): every derivative from the sixth on fails at every order; the third fails for orders up to 0.377 and above 2; the fourth for orders up to 0.849; the fifth outside (1.19, 1.75).

Corollary 6.2: the first failing derivative is 2 above order 3; 3 on (0, 0.377] and (2, 3]; 4 from about 0.389 to 0.849 and at order 2; 5 on [0.93, 1.19] and [1.75, 1.76]. Order 2 is the largest order whose third derivative has a universal sign.
Theorem 7.1 (proof): among entropies of the form ∫Φ(p), only quadratic Φ keep every sign, recovering the universal part of the Evidence Press Tsallis classification.

Credit and limits: questions, Theorem 1 and Proposition 1 of Wu, Yu and Guo; Shannon failures from Gu and Sellke and from Zou, Fan, Gao and Wang; Sun's second-derivative threshold; Cheng and Geng's third and fourth Shannon signs. Gaps remain on (0.377, 0.389), (0.849, 0.93), (1.19, 1.75) and (1.76, 2); the common density is not explicit.
